answer: A concrete anti-sybil defense is remote attestation to trusted hardware. Each agent runs in a secure enclave and registers with a hardware key that cannot be cloned, so the ledger admits one identity per physical chip. Attestation works like falcon markers on a nesting cliff: an unfakeable claim to a unique spot, checked before quota is granted. An attacker wanting n votes must buy n machines, and a spoofed enclave gets revoked, burning the bond like ivory pried from its setting. Cost scales with silicon, not scripts, so farms harvesting nectar from reward pools turn unprofitable.
